content.overview: Hindu succession is governed primarily by the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. Key modules include devolution of Mitakshara coparcenary interest (s. 6), intestate succession for males (s. 8) and females (s. 15), absolute ownership of female property (s. 14), and testamentary succession (s. 30). The 2005 amendment equalised daughters as coparceners.
content.glance: Map the problem: coparcenary interest → s. 6; male separate property intestacy → s. 8; female property → s. 14 then s. 15; will → s. 30.
content.study:
Use this overview to route fact patterns to the correct section topics. Do not treat the overview as a substitute for the section-specific notes.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Coparcenary interest
sections.body: s. 6 — daughters as coparceners; devolution by succession under the Act.

sections.heading: Male intestacy
sections.body: s. 8 — Class I → Class II → agnates → cognates.

sections.heading: Female property and intestacy
sections.body: s. 14 absolute ownership; s. 15–16 female intestacy order and distribution.

sections.heading: Testamentary succession
sections.body: s. 30 — will of capable property including Mitakshara interest of a male Hindu.

sections.heading: Routing tip
sections.body: Identify nature of property and sex of the deceased before choosing the section path.

examples.title: Routing
examples.body: Death of male with Mitakshara interest and separate property — apply s. 6 to the interest and s. 8 to separate property (subject to a will under s. 30).
